lines.text: Eliphaz the Temanite says Job once strengthened feeble hands, but now trouble has come and Job is dismayed.
Eliphaz asks who innocent has ever perished, and says those who sow trouble perish by a great flood.
In a night vision a spirit glides past Eliphaz, and a voice asks if a mortal can be more righteous than God.
Eliphaz says resentment kills a fool, whose sons are crushed in court, and the thirsty consume his harvest.
Eliphaz says he would bring his cause before God, who wounds and heals, and promises Job many offspring.
